scenes.narration: Your scanner just flagged 25 vulnerable packages. Which of them can your code actually reach?
scenes.headline: 25 alerts. Which ones matter?
scenes.caption: HTTPie 2.6.0: one dependency scan, 25 vulnerability alerts.

scenes.narration: This is HTTPie 2.6.0. Blast Radius loads the app and its pinned dependencies into a FalkorDB graph. About 7,000 functions across 11 packages. Each OSV advisory maps to the function its fix commit changed. Then we ask the graph one question. Is there a call path from an entry point to that function? There are three verdicts. 3 reachable. 22 unknown, and we say so. 0 declared safe.
scenes.headline: Ask the graph, not severity
scenes.caption: 25 alerts: 3 reachable, 22 unknown, 0 declared safe.

scenes.narration: Here is one. CVE-2023-32681 in requests. Four hops: core.main, core.program, collect_messages, Session.send, rebuild_proxies. Every claim cites a path id returned by FalkorDB. No path, no claim. Five unknowns have a possible path through dynamic dispatch. We disclose that instead of guessing.
scenes.headline: Proof is a call path
scenes.caption: CVE-2023-32681: core.main to SessionRedirectMixin.rebuild_proxies in 4 hops.

scenes.narration: Nothing is hidden. Every Cypher query streams to the Under the hood panel with its latency. About 60 queries in roughly 200 milliseconds.
scenes.headline: Every query, live
scenes.caption: Each Cypher query and its millisecond latency, streamed as it runs.

scenes.narration: Now we act. Version constraints live on DEPENDS_ON edges. Upgrading requests to 2.32.4 clears 2 reachable CVEs and passes smoke checks in a throw-away virtualenv, pip check included. urllib3 2.5.0 is blocked. Before any test runs, FalkorDB builds the upgraded graph and diffs imported names. HTTPie imports DEFAULT_CIPHERS, which no longer exists. The smoke check then confirms the ImportError.
scenes.headline: A plan the graph checks
scenes.caption: requests 2.32.4 passes. urllib3 2.5.0 blocked: DEFAULT_CIPHERS removed.

scenes.narration: The same diff shows requests-toolbelt breaks too. So the plan adds requests-toolbelt 1.0.0. The LLM drafts a minimal patch to httpie/ssl.py, applied to a copy. Smoke checks pass on that exact combination. Re-running the analysis on the upgraded graph leaves 0 reachable, down from 3. Test results are shown separately from the fixed claim. Patches are drafts. Nothing runs on the real repo.
scenes.headline: From 3 reachable to 0
scenes.caption: Draft patch applied to a copy; tests reported separately from the fix.

scenes.narration: Now the twist. The same critical CVE, PyYAML 5.3.1, CVSS 9.8, in two apps. pre-commit 2.9.0 only passes a safe loader through functools.partial. No path found. A small app using FullLoader is reachable in 2 hops. Same alert, opposite answers. Verdicts persist in a shared FalkorDB graph and are recalled across apps in the Portfolio view.
scenes.headline: Same CVE, opposite answers
scenes.caption: CVE-2020-14343: no path in pre-commit, reachable in 2 hops elsewhere.

scenes.narration: Across 3 real apps plus a control: 59 alerts, 10 reachable, 48 unknown, all disclosed. The vulnerable function is inferred from the fix commit, and we say so. Reachable is not exploitable. FalkorDB makes this work: persistent graphs, shortestPath, constraints on edges, a two-graph diff, and one shared decision graph.
scenes.headline: Why FalkorDB
scenes.caption: 3 apps plus a control: 59 alerts, 10 reachable, 48 unknown.

scenes.narration: Stop triaging by severity alone. Ask the graph for the path, then check the fix. This is Blast Radius. Try the live demo at blast-radius-yeki dot onrender dot com.
